newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares drop sharply after Wall St fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares drop sharply after Wall St fall.

text.p: Singapore's key stock market index fell sharply in opening Friday trade as the impact of an overnight 160 point fall on Wall Street hit local shares.
At 0200 GMT the key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 13.87 points at 2,140.46, recovering slightly from a 20-point plunge in the opening minutes of trading.
"The fall could take the STII down to 2,100 or even lower," said a dealer with a local firm.
Poor domestic blue chip results added to the pressure.
"The blue chips are disappointing and are being marked down to discount the poor results," said another dealer.
Dealers said buying interest was heavier in small cap stocks and shares newly listed after initial public offerings (IPOs).
"The IPOs are driving the market, but only selected ones," one broker said.

The debut of Hong Kong-based Noble Group provided a bright spot for investors -- it opened at US$1.04, an 18 percent premium on its US$0.88 offer price -- but losers outstripped gainers 178 to 42 at 0200 GMT on volume of 56.4 million shares.
Singapore Press foreign shares led the fall, down Singapore $0.50 at S$27.10 while North Borneo Timbers topped the gainers, rising S$0.25 at S$8.20.
